operational_definition.definition_text: MSS reference acceptance rule (2022-era, episode-3 framing): a short-term high break is significant only in the context that the prior move traded into liquidity below an old low; symmetric rule for lows/buy-side.
operational_definition.provenance: ICT-2022-MENTORSHIP-EP3 transcript, 'Two-minute chart review' chapter (≈4:21+): 'when this high is taken out ... that's significant only if this run down here has traded into sell stops, okay below an old [low] of some kind'.
conflicts_with: repo 2.1C: first close breach of monitored confirmed level + pre-state table (UP/DOWN/MIXED/UNDEFINED) — no liquidity precondition
common SMC restatements: 'break of the most recent swing high/low + displacement' (forexfactory TFlab threads), no liquidity precondition
LuxAlgo SMC: pivot-length structure with optional 'liquidity sweep requirement' toggle (a different precondition)

observable: short-term high exists before the low at (3)
the run-down traded under a prior low
the high was subsequently taken out on a stated candle
interpretive: 'significant only if' — a normative selection rule, not an observable

alternatives.description: Treating any short-term-high break as an MSS reference without the liquidity precondition
alternatives.source_quote_or_paraphrase: 'i see a lot of people try to teach my concepts it'll talk about market structure breaks or shifts and we'll use that term interchangeably'
alternatives.why_not_selected: Source rejects unconditional breaks; significance is context-gated.

alternatives.description: Interpreting the same break as a multi-day 'break in structure' rather than an intraday 'shift'
alternatives.source_quote_or_paraphrase: 'for intraday i want you to think about intraday market structure shifts because it's not necessarily a break in market structure that leads to prolonged multi-day movement'
alternatives.why_not_selected: Scale semantics: 'shift' = intraday draw expectation; 'break' reserved for larger context.

explanation.trader_explanation: The trader separates the factual break from its contextual acceptance and further separates 'shift' (intraday) from 'break' (multi-day) semantics — a two-level scale/context gate on the same observable event.

supporting_evidence.text: when this high is taken out right there on that candle, that's significant only if this run down here has traded into sell stops
i'm using the term market structure shift not market structure break ... an intraday shift in market structure just means that there's likely a downside draw or an upside draw intraday

task_contract.correctness_clause: 'Correct' = accepting the (4)-high break as MSS reference only when the source's liquidity precondition holds at decision time; and labeling the event an intraday 'shift', not a multi-day 'break'.
forbidden_interpretations: any close breach is an MSS

element.selection_claim: The FIRST FVG presented after the open was the entry array ('First Presented FVG'), and the draw-on-liquidity was set at the CE (midpoint) of the Opening Range Gap — a cross-scale liquidity reference (session gap midpoint) rather than a swing high/low.

operational_definition.definition_text: (a) Entry rule: one tick beyond the FVG boundary in trade direction. (b) DOL rule: CE of the ORG is the first draw after the open (2024-era teaching). 'First presented' = the first gap price offers to the trader in session sequence.
